segments.text: There's nothing more frustrating than getting a puncture. In this short film I'm going to explain how to repair a tire using the compressor and sealant kit that's provided in scot of vehicles.
Having the kit in your vehicle increases space and reduces weight. It works by distributing a sealant around the inside of the tire which seals punctures, allowing the tire to be reinflated.
We're away from the main road here and away from the main risk. So now we can start the repair. First of all, apply the parking brake to prevent the vehicle moving accidentally.
Next, ensure the gear lever is in the neutral position for both manual and automatic transmission types. And finally, make sure all passengers leave the vehicle and move to a safe area.
The kit works on punctures no more than 4mm in diameter. The kit cannot be used at the wheel rim is damaged or the vehicle has been driven with an underinflated or flat tire for an extended period.
If you can't use the puncture repair kit, you will need to arrange vehicle recovery by contacting scot of roadside assistance.
The kit comprises of a compressor unit and a sealant kit which also has a valve tool, spare tire valve and warning sticker in the back.
Now take the warning sticker and place it into the driver's field of view.
Then take the sealant bottle and give it a good shake. Make sure it's all mixed up and then attach the filler tube to it like this and make sure it pierces the foil.
Now we remove the valve cap from the tire valve itself. And using the removal tool, pop it into the valve, unscrew and remove the valve completely.
Don't worry about losing the valve as you have a spare one in the kit. Now we get the fluid and attach the filler tube to the tire valve.

Hold the sealant bottle upside down and fill the complete content into the tire. It doesn't matter where the tire valve is located when the vehicle is stationary, as the sealant will work its way around the tire when the vehicle is driven.
Disconnect the filler tube from the tire valve and refit the valve insert back into the valve using the removal tool until it's tight.
Now we take the compressor which is this item here and open up the front cover which gives you access to the electric which plug into the 12 volt socket inside your car.
And also the inflatient tube that will attach to the actual tire itself. Now we attach the tube to the tire valve like this.
Connect this section to your 12 volt socket and then start your engine.
Turn the compressor on by the switch here.
The tire will start to inflate. Keep an eye on the gauge for pressures. These can be found on the inside of your owner's manual or on the inside of your fuel filler flap.
We will take a few minutes to inflate. If the pressure stays below the required level, try the car a few meters to spread the sealant around the tire.
If it consistently stays low and the tires too badly damaged and you will need to arrange the recovery.
Once inflated to the right pressure, you can disconnect the tube, pop your tire valve cover back on and drive straight off.
There are a couple of important points that you should be aware of when first driving off.
The tire sealant will move around inside the tire so it is absolutely vital that you stop after 10 minutes and check the tire pressure using the gauge.
If the tire drops below the pressure is outlined in the owner handbook, then it could be that the tire is too badly damaged.
If it is okay, then you can drive on. But first remember these points.
The sealant means that you can drive at a maximum speed of 50 miles per hour. Accelerate, break and corner gently.
It is a temporary measure. So please see your local Scoda Retailer or tire Retailer immediately who can repair or replace the damaged tire.
So I hope that has shown you just how easy it is to use the tire repair kit.
But please remember this film is to be used as a guide and you must read the instruction manual thoroughly before using the kit.
And of course, if you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact your local Scoda Retailer.
Thanks for watching this short film.
